To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NF-kB (a transcription factor that promotes several antiapoptosis genes) is activated (detected in the nucleus) in prostate cancer and its activation is related to higher PSA levels.

the NF-kB transcription factor is expressed in normal prostate, benign prostatic hyperlasia (BPH) as well as in prostate cancer, and that its expression is related with the serum levels of PSA in all three conditions.

the activation of NF-kB in prostate cancer could explain the elevated serum levels of prostate specific antigen (PSA) and that the blockage of NF-kB could be used as therapeutic target in prostate cancer.

the study of the role of NF-kB as a transcription factor in the development of prostatic disease, with a special emphasis on the relation with PSA levels.
the study of the role of NF-kB and its relation with PSA serum levels in prostate diseases.
the study of the role of NF-kB in prostate disease and its relationship with serum levels of PSA, both in normal individuals and in those with prostate disease.
